224.text:
Assertion : Deforestation is one main factor contributing to global warming.
Reason : Besides $\mathrm{CO}_2$, two other gases methane and CFCs are also included under green house gases.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
224.sol:
Deforestation increases atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$ content by releasing carbon stored in organic matter and reduced primary productivity. So deforestation is one of the main factors contributing to global
warming other than green house gases. The various green house gases are $\mathrm{CO}_2(60 \%$ warming effect), $\mathrm{CH}_4$ (20\% warming effect) CFC ( $14 \%$ warming effect) and nitrogen oxide $\left(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}, 6 \%\right.$ warming effect). Due to increase of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration, the absorption of heat radiation also increase thus increasing the temperature. This increase in temperature may causes melting of glacier and polar ice caps, which is called global warming. This melting of glaciers and polar ice results in raising the sea level. Actually these green house gases absorbs infra red radiations (heat) of the sun like glass and thus traps the heat and does not allow it to radiate back to the space. They instead radiate the heat back to earth, thus causing increase in temperature.

1891.subject: Zoology
1891.text:
Assertion: Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA to produce sticky ends.
Reason : Stickiness of the ends facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA polymerase.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1891.sol: Restriction enzyme, a type of endonuclease, functions by "inspecting" the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds a recognition sequence, it binds and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific point leaving single stranded portions at the ends. This results in overhanging stretches called sticky ends. These are named so because they form hydrogen bonds with their complementary counter parts, i.e., they can join similar complementary ends of DNA fragment from some other source with the help of DNA ligase. This stickiness of the ends facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA ligase, not DNA polymerase.

1929.subject: Zoology
1929.text:
Assertion : On touching radial artery in our wrist, we feel pulse waves.
Reason : The heart beats originate from the sinoatrial node (SA node) on the right atrium.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
1929.sol: Pulse is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation in the aorta and its main arteries. It is a regular jerk of an artery. The pulse rate is exactly the same as the heart rate because an artery pulses every time the heart beats. Pulse is usually taken on the radial artery in the wrist but it can be taken on any artery that flows near enough to the surface of the body to be felt. The heart beat originates from the sinoatrial node (SA Node) - pacemaker, which lies in the wall of the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava. The SA node is a mass of neuromuscular tissue. Another mass of neuromuscular tissue, the atrioventricular node (AV node) is situated in the wall of the right atrium. The AV node picks up the wave of contraction propagated by SA node. A mass of specialized fibres, the bundle of His, originates from the AV node. The bundle of His divides into two branches, one going to each ventricle. Within the myocardium of the ventricles, the branches of bundle of His divides into a network of fine fibres called the Purkinje fibres. The bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres convey impulse of contraction from the AV node to the myocardium of the ventricles.

NaOH is in excess since 0.05 moles of NaOH react with 0.04 moles of HCl

The total volume after mixing -100 ml of $\mathrm{HCl}+100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $\mathrm{NaOH}+800 \mathrm{ml}$ of distilled water $\Rightarrow 1000 \mathrm{ml}$ or 1 L so the concentration of $\mathrm{NaOH}=\frac{0.01 \mathrm{moles}}{1 \mathrm{I}}=0.01 \mathrm{ m}\mathrm{pOH}=-\log \left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]\mathrm{pOH}=-\log [0.01]=2$
As we know pH + pOH=14
$\mathrm{pH}=14-\mathrm{pOH}=14-2=12$

\(\begin{aligned}
& \text{Since, }\left|\begin{array}{ll}f(x) & f^{\prime}(x) \\
f^{\prime}(x) & f^{\prime \prime}(x)

& \Rightarrow \quad f(x) f^{\prime \prime}(x)-\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f(x) f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{f^{\prime \prime}(x)}{f^{\prime}(x)}=\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}\\
\end{aligned}\)
On, integrating both sides, we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{f^{\prime \prime}(x)}{f^{\prime}(x)}d x=\int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log _e\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)=\log _e(f(x))+c \\
 \text{ and }  \because \quad f(0)=1 \text{ and }f^{\prime}(0)=2 \\
 \text{ and }  \therefore \quad c=\log _e 2 \\
 \text{ and }  \log _e\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)=\log _e(f(x))+\log _e 2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=2 f(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}d x=\int2 d x \Rightarrow \log _e f(x)=2 x+c \\
& \because \quad f(0)=1 \text{, so }c=0 \\
& \because \quad \log _e f(x)=2 x \Rightarrow f(x)=e^{2 x} \\
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (1) is correct.

Let $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ and $\left(x_2, y_2\right)$ be the end points of a focal chord.

Since, $t_1 t_2=-1$ as $t_1 and t_2$ are the end points of a focal chord

Now, $x_1 x_2=\frac{25}{16}$ and $y_1 y_2=-\frac{25}{4}\begin{aligned}& \therefore \quad 4 x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2=4\left(\frac{25}{16}\right)-\frac{25}{4}\\
& \frac{25}{4}-\frac{25}{4}=0
\end{aligned}$

put $y = 0$

$⇒ \left(af^{2} + ch^{2}\right)2 - 4f^{2}ach^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(af^{2} - ch^{2}\right)2 = 0$

$⇒ af^{2} = ch^{2} . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

So from equation $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) & \left(3\right) we can say that& $abc = 2fgh$& is incorrect.

Hence,

Subtracting $\left(iv\right)$ from $\left(i\right)$, we get

$\alpha = 1$

Putting in $\left(iii\right) \text{ and } \left(iv\right)$, we get

$2\beta + 3\gamma = - 9 . . . \left(v\right)$

$\beta + \gamma = - 1 . . . \left(vi\right)$

On solving, we get $\gamma = - 7 \text{ and } \beta = 6$

Therefore,

${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + {\gamma}^{2} = 86$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} $\cdot \left(9\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{9}{2}\overset{^}{k}\right) =27 + 15 + \dfrac{63}{2}

$⇒ $\left($ x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right)$\cdot \left(9\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{9}{2}\overset{^}{k}\right) =42 + \dfrac{63}{2}

$⇒ 9x + 3y + $\dfrac{9}{2}$ z = $\dfrac{147}{2}

$⇒ 3x + y + $\dfrac{3}{2}$ z = $\dfrac{49}{2}

$⇒ 6x + 2y + 3z = 49$.

15255.text: A short bar magnet placed in a horizontal plane has its axis aligned along north-south direction. Null points are found on the axis of the magnet at $20 \mathrm{ cm}$ from the centre of magnet. The earth's magnetic field at the place is $B$ and angle of dip is $0^{{}^{\circ}}$. If the total magnetic field on the normal bisector of the magnet $20 \mathrm{ cm}$ from the centre of the magnet is $0.6 \mathrm{G}$, then the magnitude of $B$ is.
15255.sol:
At null point (and along the axis), earth's magnetic field and bar's magnetic field are opposite in direction.
On equitorial line, bar's mågnetic field is opposite in idirection to its field on the axis. Hence, on equatorial line, the two fields add up As null points are on the axis of the bar magnet, therefore,
$B_1=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 M}{d^3}=H$
on the equitorial line of magnet at same distance (d), field due to the magnet is
$B_2=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{M}{d^3}=\frac{B_1}{2}=\frac{H}{2}$
Therefore, total magnetic field at this point on equitorial line is
$B=B_2+H=\frac{3 H}{2}=\frac{3}{2} \times H$
Since, given $B=0.69$
$0.6=\frac{3}{2} \times H \Rightarrow H=\frac{0.6 \times 2}{3}=0.4 \mathrm{G}$

19687.subject: Chemistry
19687.text:
Pick out the incorrect statement(s) from the following.
1. Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose.
2. $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose are anomers.
3. $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose are enantiomers.
4. Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide made of only $\beta$-D-glucose units.
5. Starch is a mixture of amylase and amylopectin, both contain unbranched chain of $\alpha$-D-glucose units.
19687.sol:
Statement 1 is correct: Glucose exists in two crystalline forms, $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose, which differ in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at the C-1 carbon.

Statement 2 is correct: $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose are anomers because they differ only in the configuration at the anomeric carbon (C-1).

Statement 3 is incorrect: $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose are diastereomers, not enantiomers. Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, whereas anomers are a specific type of diastereomer.

Statement 4 is correct: Cellulose is a linear polysaccharide composed of $\beta$-D-glucose units linked by $\beta$-1,4-glycosidic bonds.

Statement 5 is incorrect: Starch is a mixture of amylose and amylopectin. Amylose is an unbranched chain of $\alpha$-D-glucose units, but amylopectin is a branched-chain polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units containing $\alpha$-1,4 and $\alpha$-1,6-glycosidic linkages. Therefore, the statement that both contain unbranched chains is false.

The incorrect statements are 3 and 5.

Answer: 3 and 5 only

20081.subject: Chemistry
20081.text: Choose the incorrect statement from the following
options: $\mathrm{Cu}$ (I) compounds in aqueous medium undergo disproportionation reaction
$\mathrm{MoO}_3$ and $\mathrm{WO}_3$ are not as strong oxidants as $\mathrm{CrO}_3$
The ability of Fluorine to stabilise the higher oxidation states of transition metals exceeds that of Oxygen
$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$
20081.sol:
(1) Correct: $Cu^+$ is unstable in aqueous medium due to the much higher hydration energy of $Cu^{2+}$. It undergoes disproportionation: $2Cu^+(aq) \to Cu^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$.

(2) Correct: Oxidising power decreases down Group 6. $CrO_3$ is a strong oxidant while $MoO_3$ and $WO_3$ are much weaker.

(3) Incorrect: Oxygen can stabilise higher oxidation states through multiple bonding (e.g., in oxoanions like $MnO_4^-$, $CrO_4^{2-}$). The ability of oxygen to stabilise higher oxidation states is superior to that of fluorine in many cases. So the statement that fluorine exceeds oxygen is incorrect.

(4) Correct: $Cr^{2+}(d^4)$ is oxidised to $Cr^{3+}(d^3$, stable $t_{2g}^3)$. $E°(Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}) = -0.41$ V, while $E°(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = +0.77$ V. Lower reduction potential means $Cr^{2+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Fe^{2+}$.

The incorrect statement is (3).

20294.subject: Chemistry
20294.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
20294.text: The reducing agent which is used to reduce iron oxide in blast furnace is
20294.sol:
In the blast furnace, iron oxides such as $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ are reduced to metallic iron. The process involves two main reducing agents: coke ($\mathrm{C}$) and carbon monoxide ($\mathrm{CO}$).

Coke acts as the primary fuel and also reacts with oxygen to form $\mathrm{CO_2}$, which is then reduced by more coke to form $\mathrm{CO}$ according to the reaction $\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}$.

The carbon monoxide ($\mathrm{CO}$) is the actual chemical reducing agent that reduces the iron oxides in the upper, cooler parts of the furnace, for example: $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 3\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO_2}$.

While coke is the source of the reducing agent, $\mathrm{CO}$ is the primary reducing agent that performs the reduction of iron oxides in the blast furnace.

Answer: $\mathrm{CO}$

21096.subject: Mathematics
21096.text: The coefficient of $x^{20}$ in the expansion of $\left(1+3 x+3 x^2+x^3\right)^{20}$ is
21096.sol:
The given expression is $(1 + 3x + 3x^2 + x^3)^{20}$.

Observe that $1 + 3x + 3x^2 + x^3 = (1 + x)^3$.

Substituting this into the expression, we get $((1 + x)^3)^{20} = (1 + x)^{60}$.

The general term in the binomial expansion of $(1 + x)^{60}$ is given by ^{60}C_{r} x^{r}$.

To find the coefficient of $x^{20}$, we set $r = 20$.

The coefficient is ^{60}C_{20}$.

Using the property ^{n}C_{r} = ^{n}C_{n-r}$, we have ^{60}C_{20} = ^{60}C_{60-20} = ^{60}C_{40}$.

Answer: $\binom{60}{40}$

22448.subject: Physics
22448.text: The wavelength of the second line of Balmer series is $486.4 \mathrm{ nm}$. What is the wavelength of the first line of Lyman series?
22448.sol:
The Rydberg formula for the wavelength $\lambda$ of a spectral line in a hydrogen-like atom is given by $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right) Z^2$. For hydrogen, $Z = 1$.

The second line of the Balmer series corresponds to the transition from $n_2 = 4 to n_1 = 2$. Thus, $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_B} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{4^2} \right) = R \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{16} \right) =$ R $\left( \dfrac{3}{16} \right). Given $\lambda_B = 486.4 $\text{ nm}, we have $ R = $\dfrac{16}{3 \times 486.4} \text{ nm}^{-1}.

The first line$ of the Lyman series corresponds to the transition from n_2 = 2 to n_1 = 1$. Thus, \dfrac{1}{\lambda_L} =$ R $\left( \dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{2^2} \right) =$ R $\left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} \right) = R \left( \dfrac{3}{4} \right).

Substituting$ the value of R$: \dfrac{1}{\lambda_L} = \left( \dfrac{16}{3 \times 486.4} \right) \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{4}{486.4} = \dfrac{1}{121.6}.

Therefore, $\lambda_L = 121.6 $\text{ nm}.

Answer: 121.6 \mathrm{ nm}$

22667.subject: Physics
22667.text: A monochromatic beam of photons of intensity to 1.5 $Wm^{-2}$ and energy 11.2 eV is incident on a material of work function 4.8 eV. What is the maximum speed of photoelectrons emitted due to photoelectric effect if, only 0.53% of the incident photons eject photoelectrons. Given mass of electron $m = 9 \times 10^{-31}$ kg.
22667.sol:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$K_{\max} = E - \Phi$

Substituting the given values for the energy of the incident photon and the work function:

$K_{\max} = 11.2 \text{ eV} - 4.8 \text{ eV} = 6.4 \text{ eV}$

Converting the maximum kinetic energy into Joules:

$K_{\max} = 6.4 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J} = 10.24 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$

The maximum kinetic energy is related to the maximum speed by $K_{\max} = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_{\max}^2$.

$v_{\max} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 K_{\max}}{m}}$

Substituting the mass of the electron $m = 9 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$:

$v_{\max} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 10.24 \times 10^{-19}}{9 \times 10^{-31}}}$

$v_{\max} = \sqrt{\dfrac{20.48 \times 10^{12}}{9}}$

$v_{\max} = \dfrac{4.525}{3} \times 10^6 \approx 1.5 \times 10^6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.5 \times 10^6\ ms^{-1}$

27195.text:
Total number of alkali insoluble solid sulphonamides obtained by reaction of given amines with Hinsberg's reagent is $\_\_\_\_$.
Aniline, N-Methylaniline, Methanamine, N, N-Dimethylmethanamine, N-Methyl methanamine, Phenylmethanamine, N-propylaniline, N-phenylaniline, N, N-Dimethylaniline, Allyl amine, Isopropyl amine
27195.sol:
Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulfonyl chloride) classifies amines by their reaction products:
Primary amines (RNH₂) form alkali-soluble sulfonamides (soluble in NaOH).
Secondary amines (R₂NH) form alkali-insoluble sulfonamides (precipitate in NaOH).
Tertiary amines (R₃N) do not react.
Analyzing the given amines:
Aniline (primary), Methanamine (primary), Phenylmethanamine (primary), Allyl amine (primary), Isopropyl amine (primary) → alkali-soluble.
N,N-Dimethylmethanamine (tertiary), N,N-Dimethylaniline (tertiary) → no reaction.
N-Methylaniline (secondary), N-Methyl methanamine (secondary), N-Propylaniline (secondary), N-Phenylaniline (secondary) → alkali-insoluble.
Total alkali-insoluble sulfonamides: 4.

Consider the following chemical equilibrium of the gas phase reaction at a constant temperature :
$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{~g})$
If $p$ being the total pressure, $K_p$ is the pressure equilibrium constant and $\alpha$ is the degree of dissociation, then which of the following is true at equilibrium?

a moles of $A(g)$ taken initially and at time Now moles fraction of $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}), \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) and \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$ are
$\begin{aligned}
& X_A=\frac{a-a \alpha}{a+a \alpha}=\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha} \\
& X_B=\frac{a \alpha}{a+a \alpha}=\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha} \\
& X_C=\frac{a \alpha}{a+a \alpha}=\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}
\end{aligned}$
Now if $P$ is total pressure then partial pressure o $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}), \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$ are
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P} \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P} \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{C}}=\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P} \\
& \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P}}{\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) \mathrm{P}} \\
& \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\alpha^2 \mathrm{P}}{1-\alpha^2}
\end{aligned}$
As $K_P$ is only function of temperature.

28198.text: For a reaction taking place in three steps at same temperature, overall rate constant $K = \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{3}}$. If ${Ea}_{1}, {Ea}_{2}$ and ${Ea}_{3}$ are $40, 50$ and $60kJ / mol$ respectively, the overall $Ea$ is _________ $kJ / mol$.
28198.sol:
According to Arrhenius concept,

$K = {Ae}^{- {E}_{a} / RT}$

Given that,

${K}_{} = \left({K}_{1} . {K}_{2}\right) / {K}_{3}$

Using Arrhenius equation we can expand above equation as

${e}^{- {E}_{a ( net )} / RT} = \dfrac{{e}^{- {E}_{a1} / RT} \times {e}^{- {E}_{a2} / RT}}{{e}^{- {E}_{a3} / RT}}$

Hence,

 ${E}_{a ( net )} = {E}_{a1} + {E}_{a2} - {E}_{a3} ⇒ {E}_{a ( net )} = 40 + 50 - 60 = 30kJ / mol$

31326.subject: Chemistry
31326.text:
Total number of species from the following which can undergo disproportionation reaction ___________.
${H}_{2}{O}_{2}, {ClO}_{3}^{-}, {P}_{4}, {Cl}_{2}, Ag, {Cu}^{+ 1}, {F}_{2}, {NO}_{2}, {K}^{+}$
31326.sol:
The compounds or ions or elements in which central atom has intermediate oxidation state undergo a disproportionation reaction.

Disproportionation reactions are the reactions in which the same element/compound gets oxidised and reduced simultaneously.

1)${Cu}^{+} \to {Cu}^{2 +} + Cu$

2) $2{H}_{2}\overset{- 1}{O}2\overset{}{\to}{H}_{2}\overset{- 2}{O} + \overset{0}{O}2$

$3 ) 3{Cl}_{2} + 6{OH}^{-} \to 5{Cl}^{-} + {{ClO}_{3}}^{-} + 3{H}_{2}O$

$4 ) 2{NO}_{2} ( g ) + 2{OH}^{-} ( aq ) \to {{NO}_{2}}^{-} ( aq ) + {H}_{2}O ( l ) + {{NO}_{3}}^{-}$

$5 ) {P}_{4} + 3{OH}^{-} + 3{H}_{2}O \to {PH}_{3} + 3{H}_{2}{{PO}_{2}}^{-}$

Here, the chlorine reactant is in oxidation state $0$, and if we look at the products, the chlorine in the Cl− ion has an oxidation number of $- 1$, where it has undergone reduction. Meanwhile, the oxidation number of the chlorine in the ${{ClO}_{3}}^{-}$ ion is $+ 5$, which means it has been oxidised.

Hence, ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}, {Cu}^{+}, {Cl}_{2}, {ClO}_{3}, {P}_{4}, {NO}_{2}$ shows disproportionation reaction.

$2 . 0 = ix1 . 86 \times \dfrac{7 \times 1000}{93 \times 42}$

$2 . 0 = i\left[3 . 33\right]$

$i = 0 . 6$

$i = 1 + \left[\dfrac{1}{n} - 1\right]\beta$

$0 . 6 = 1 + \left[\dfrac{1}{2} - 1\right]\beta$

$\beta = 0 . 8$

$\left(\text{P} + \dfrac{\text{a}}{{\text{V}}^{2}}\right) \left(\text{V} - \text{b}\right) = \text{RT}$

At low pressure, the characteristic constant (a) becomes significant whereas (b) becomes negligible. So (b) is ignored.

$\left(\text{P} + \dfrac{\text{a}}{{\text{V}}^{2}}\right) \left(\text{V}\right) = \text{RT}$

$\text{PV} + \dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{V}} = \text{RT}$

At low pressure for most gases z < 1.

${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots . . , {x}_{20}$ are in G.P with common difference $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and first term as $3$

$= \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2} + {\left(i\right)}^{2} - 2{x}_{i}i$

Now $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{9\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{20}\right)}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = 12\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{40}}\right)$

And $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{i}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 20 \times 21 \times 41 = 2870$

And $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{x}_{i}i = 3 + 2 . 3\dfrac{1}{2} + 3 . 3\dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} + 4 . 3\dfrac{1}{{2}^{3}} + \ldots \ldots . AGP$

$= 6\left(4 - \dfrac{11}{{2}^{18}}\right)$

So, mean of the new data will be,

$x = \dfrac{12 - \dfrac{12}{{2}^{40}} + 2870 - 6\left(4 - \dfrac{11}{{2}^{18}}\right)}{20}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2858}{20} + \left(\dfrac{- 12}{{2}^{40}} + \dfrac{66}{{2}^{18}}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{20}$

Now $⇒ \left[x\right] = \left[142 . 4 + 0 . 00001\right] = 142$

37540.sol:

${f}_{i}$ $k + 2$ $2k$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} + 1$ $k - 3$

Now we know that,

$\text{Mean} = \dfrac{∑ {X}_{i}{f}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{2k + 2{k}^{2} – 2 + 3{k}^{2} – 3 + 4{k}^{2} + 4 + 5k – 15}{62}$

And $∑ {f}_{i} = 62$

$⇒ 3{k}^{2} + 4k - 2 = 62$

$⇒ 3{k}^{2} + 4k - 64 = 0$

$⇒ ( 3k + 16 ) ( k - 4 ) = 0$

$⇒ k = 4$

Now putting the value of $k$ in above equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\mu = \dfrac{156}{62}$

Now finding variance we get,

${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {\left({X}_{i}\right)}^{2}{f}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}} - {\left(\text{Mean}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(2k\right) + 4\left({k}^{2} - 1\right) + 9\left({k}^{2} - 1\right) + 16\left({k}^{2} + 1\right) + 25\left(k - 3\right)}{62} - {\left(\dfrac{156}{62}\right)}^{2}$

Now putting the value of $k$ in above equation we get,

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{500}{62} - {\mu}^{2}$

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} + {\mu}^{2} = \dfrac{500}{62}$

$⇒ \left[{\sigma}^{2} + {\mu}^{2}\right] = 8$

38036.text: Let a line $L$ pass through the point $P ( 2, 3, 1 )$ and be parallel to the line $x + 3y - 2z - 2 = 0 = x - y + 2z$. If the distance of $L$ from the point $( 5, 3, 8 )$ is $\alpha$, then $3{\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to ________
38036.sol:
Given,

$x + 3y - 2z - 2 = 0 = x - y + 2z$

Now direction ratio is given by,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 3 & - 2 \\ 1 & - 1 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

So, Equation of line will be $\dfrac{x - 2}{4} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = k$

Let $Q$ be $( 5, 3, 8 )$ and foot of $⊥$ from $Q$ on this line be $R$

Now, $R ≡ ( k + 2, - k + 3, - k + 1 )$

So, direction ratio of $QR$ will be ($k - 3, - k, - k - 7$),

Now using the perpendicular condition we get,

$( 1 ) ( k - 3 ) + ( - 1 ) ( - k ) + ( - 1 ) ( - k - 7 ) = 0$

$⇒ k = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

So, ${\alpha}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{13}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{17}{3}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{474}{9}$

$⇒ 3{\alpha}^{2} = 158$

38796.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac source of $220V, 50Hz$. The circuit contain a resistance $R = 100Ω$ and an inductor of inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = 79 . 6Ω$. 38796.sol:
The average rate at which energy supplied i.e. power delivered is maximum in case of the resonance, therefore

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = 79 . 6Ω$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{\omega \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{2\pif \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{100\pi \times 79 . 6} = 40\mu F$

Hence, $C = 40\mu F$.

39914.subject: Physics
39914.text: An electron is travelling with a velocity $v$ in free space and when it enters a medium, its velocity is reduced by $20\%$. The de Broglie wavelength of electron in the medium is $\alpha\lambda_0$, where $\lambda_0$ is its de Broglie wavelength in free space. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
39914.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength of an electron in free space is given by $\lambda_0 = \dfrac{h}{mv}$.

When the electron enters the medium, its velocity is reduced by $20\%$. The new velocity is $v' = v - 0.20v = 0.80v$.

The de Broglie wavelength in the medium is $\lambda' = \dfrac{h}{mv'}$.

Substituting $v' = 0.80v$, we get $\lambda' = \dfrac{h}{m(0.80v)} = \dfrac{1}{0.80} \left(\dfrac{h}{mv}\right).

Since \dfrac{1}{0.80} = \dfrac{100}{80} = 1.25$, we have $\lambda' = 1.25\lambda_0$.

Comparing this with $\lambda' = \alpha\lambda_0$, we get $\alpha = 1.25$.

Answer: $1.25$

${E}_{- q} = \dfrac{Kq}{{D}^{2} + 4{d}^{2}}{cos ⁡ \theta}_{2} \times 2$
The field due to $+ q$ is towards right and the field due to $- q$ is towards left. Also ${\theta}_{1} \approx 0$ and ${\theta}_{2} \approx 0$ .
$∴ {E}_{net} = {E}_{+ q} - {E}_{- q} \approx \dfrac{Kq}{{D}^{2} + {d}^{2}} - \dfrac{Kq}{{D}^{2} + 4{d}^{2}}$
$= \dfrac{Kq3{d}^{2}}{\left({D}^{2} + {d}^{2}\right)\left({D}^{2} + 4{d}^{2}\right)} \approx \dfrac{3Kq{d}^{2}}{{D}^{4}}$
$E ∝ \dfrac{1}{{D}^{4}}$

40977.text: The energy required to take a satellite to a height $$h$above the Earth surface (radius of Earth $= 6.4 \times {10}^{3}km$ ) is ${E}_{1}$, and the kinetic energy required for the satellite to be in a circular orbit at this height is ${E}_{2} .$ The value of $h$ for which ${E}_{1}$ and ${E}_{2}$ are equal, is$
40977.sol:
${U}_{surface} + {E}_{1} = {U}_{h}$

$KE$ of satellite is zero at earth surface and at height $h$

$- \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} + {E}_{1} = - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}$

${E}_{1} = G{M}_{e}m\left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{e}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{e} + h}\right)$

${E}_{1} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)} \times \dfrac{h}{{R}_{e}}$

Gravitational attraction ${F}_{G} = m{a}_{C} = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}^{2}}$

$m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}$

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{2\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}$

${E}_{1} = {E}_{2}$

$\dfrac{h}{{R}_{e}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ h = \dfrac{{R}_{e}}{2} = 3200km$

44514.text: A train is moving on a straight track with speed $20m{s}^{- 1}$ . It is blowing its whistle at the frequency of $1000Hz$. The percentage change in the frequency heard by a person standing near the track as the train passes him is (speed of sound $= 320m{s}^{- 1}$ ) close to:

Before train passes

${f}^{′} = \left(\dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{s}}\right) \times {f}_{0}$

$= \left(\dfrac{320}{320 - 20}\right) \times {f}_{0}$

$= \left(\dfrac{320}{300}\right) \times {f}_{0}$

$= \dfrac{16{f}_{0}}{15}$

After train passes

${f}^{′′} = \left(\dfrac{v}{v + {v}_{s}}\right) \times {f}_{0}$

${f}^{′′} = \left(\dfrac{320}{320 + 20}\right){f}_{0}$

$= \left(\dfrac{320}{340}\right){f}_{0}$

$= \left(\dfrac{16}{17}\right){f}_{0}$

Change in frequency

$= \left(\dfrac{16}{15} - \dfrac{16}{17}\right){f}_{0}$

$∴$ Percentage change in frequency

$= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{16}{15} - \dfrac{16}{17}\right){f}_{0}}{{f}_{0}} \times 100 \approx 12%$ nearly

52752.text: Whose name is not associated with the development of periodic table?
52752.sol:
Prout's gave unitary theory for the development of periodic table. He suggested that the atoms of all the element are made up of hydrogen atom.
Newlands gave law of octaves: According to him, "If elef̂ents are arranged in the increasing order of their atomic weights, the eighth element starting from the given one is the repetition of the first like the eighth node in an octave of music. Lother Meyer's plotted the atomic volumes (i.e., at. wt/density) of various elements against their atomic weight and pointed out that the similar element occupy similar position on the curve.

57140.subject: Chemistry
57140.text: Identify the aldehyde from following so that the aldehydic group is NOT attached with any $sp^3$ hybrid 'c' atom.
57140.sol:
Methanal is $H-CHO$. The aldehydic group ($-CHO$) is attached to a hydrogen atom, not to any carbon atom. Therefore, it is not attached to any $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Ethanal is $CH_3-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a methyl group, which contains an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

2-Methylpropanal is $(CH_3)_2CH-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Propanal is $CH_3-CH_2-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH_2$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Thus, methanal is the only aldehyde among the given options where the aldehydic group is not attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

57796.text:
Which of the following compounds is formed as major product in the following reaction.
$\text{ 2-methylbut-2-ene } \xrightarrow[\text{ Peroxide }]{\mathrm{HBr}} $$\text{ Product }$
57796.sol:
Free radical addition of HBr to 2-methylbut-2-ene in the presence of peroxide follows the anti-Markovnikov pathway.

The reaction proceeds via a radical mechanism initiated by peroxide.
HBr adds across the double bond with the bromine radical attaching to the less substituted carbon to form a more stable tertiary radical intermediate.

$\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3 + Br^\bullet \rightarrow CH_3-\overset{\bullet}{C}(CH_3)-CHBr-CH_3}$

The tertiary radical then abstracts a hydrogen from HBr to yield the final product.
$\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\bullet}{C}(CH_3)-CHBr-CH_3 + HBr \rightarrow CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CHBr-CH_3 + Br^\bullet}$

The product is 3-bromo-2-methylbutane.

57797.subject: Chemistry
57797.text: Identify the product obtained when alkenes are oxidised with $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ in dil. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$.
57797.sol:
Strong oxidative cleavage of alkenes with potassium permanganate in dilute sulfuric acid cleaves carbon-carbon double bonds. The products depend on substitution patterns: vinylic carbons with hydrogen atoms oxidize to carboxylic acids (alkanoic acids), while fully substituted vinylic carbons oxidize to ketones (alkanones).

Under these strongly oxidizing conditions, alkanals (aldehydes) are unstable intermediates that undergo further oxidation to carboxylic acids. Alkanols are not formed, as they result from milder oxidation conditions. While both alkanones and alkanoic acids may be produced depending on substrate structure, alkanoic acids represent the most general and stable oxidation product.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

58414.text:
What is the name of monomer used in the formation of a polymer
?
58414.sol:
The repeating unit $\text{–CH}_2\text{–C(CH}_3)\text{=CH–CH}_2\text{–}$ indicates 1,4-addition polymerization of a conjugated diene.

Reversing the polymerization by breaking the terminal single bonds and reforming the conjugated system yields the monomer $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3)\text{–CH=CH}_2$, known as isoprene.

Comparing with options: tetrafluoroethylene ($\text{CF}_2\text{=CF}_2$) forms Teflon; acrylonitrile ($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH–CN}$) forms polyacrylonitrile; caprolactam undergoes ring-opening polymerization to form Nylon-6. Only isoprene corresponds to the given structure.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

58807.subject: Chemistry
58807.text: Calculate the number of atoms present in $1\ \text{g}$ metal that forms simple unit cell structure if product of density and volume of unit cell is $66.5 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{g}$
58807.sol:
For a simple cubic unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 1$.

The mass of one unit cell is equal to the product of its density and volume.

Mass of one unit cell = $\rho \times V = 66.5 \times 10^{-24} \text{ g}$.

Since there is $1$ atom per unit cell, the mass of one atom is $66.5 \times 10^{-24} \text{ g}$.

The number of atoms in $1 \text{ g}$ of the metal is given by:

Number of atoms = $\dfrac{\text{Total mass}}{\text{Mass of one atom}}$

Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{66.5 \times 10^{-24}}$

Number of atoms = $0.015037 \times 10^{24}$

Number of atoms $\approx 1.504 \times 10^{22}$

59091.text: van't Hoff factor for $\text{BaCl}_2$ is $2.47$, calculate the percentage dissociation of in its aqueous solution.
59091.sol:
The dissociation reaction of $\text{BaCl}_2$ is:

$\text{BaCl}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{Ba}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-}$

The number of ions produced per formula unit, $n = 3$.

The relation between van't Hoff factor $i$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is:

$i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha$

Substituting the given values:

$2.47 = 1 + (3 - 1)\alpha$

$2.47 = 1 + 2\alpha$

$2\alpha = 1.47$

$\alpha = 0.735$

Percentage dissociation $= \alpha \times 100 = 73.5\%$

61335.text: The differential equation satisfied by $y=X \sin (6 t+5)+Y \cos (6 t+5)$ is (where $X$ and $Y$ are constants)
61335.sol:
Given the function

$y = X \sin(6t + 5) + Y \cos(6t + 5)$

Differentiate twice to find a relation with the original function.

Differentiating $y$ yields the first derivative:

$\frac{dy}{dt} = 6X \cos(6t + 5) - 6Y \sin(6t + 5)$

A second differentiation gives:

$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = -36X \sin(6t + 5) - 36Y \cos(6t + 5)$

This simplifies to:

$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = -36 \left(X \sin(6t + 5) + Y \cos(6t + 5)\right)$

Recognizing the original definition of $y$, we substitute to obtain:

$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = -36y$

Rearranged, this gives the homogeneous second-order linear differential equation:

$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} +36y = 0$

This corresponds to option C, so the final answer is $\boxed{C}$

61699.subject: Mathematics
61699.text: If $x=\sin \theta, y=\sin ^3 \theta$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$ at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$ is
61699.sol:
To compute the second derivative $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}$ for the parametric equations $x = \sin \theta$ and $y = \sin^{3} \theta$, begin by finding the first derivative. Using the chain rule, $\frac{d y}{d x} = \frac{d y/d \theta}{d x/d \theta} = \frac{3 \sin^{2} \theta \cos \theta}{\cos \theta} = 3 \sin^{2} \theta$, valid for $\cos \theta \neq 0$.

For the second derivative, apply $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} = \frac{d}{d \theta} \left( \frac{d y}{d x} \right) \cdot \frac{d \theta}{d x}$. Differentiating gives $\frac{d}{d \theta} (3 \sin^{2} \theta) = 6 \sin \theta \cos \theta$ and $\frac{d \theta}{d x} = \frac{1}{\cos \theta}$, so $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} = 6 \sin \theta$.

At $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}$, this evaluates to $6 \sin \left( \frac{\pi}{6} \right) = 6 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 3$.

The second derivative at this point is $\boxed{3}$.

62940.text: Negation of the statement "If an integer is greater than 4 and less than 5, then it is a multiple of 3", is
options: An integer is not greater than 4 but less than 5 and it is a multiple of 3.
If an integer is not greater than 4 and less than 5 then it is not a multiple of 3.
An integer is greater than 4 and less than 5 but it is not a multiple of 3.
An integer is not greater than 4 and not less than 5 but it is not a multiple of 3.
62940.sol:
Let $p$ be the statement "An integer is greater than 4 and less than 5".

Let $q$ be the statement "it is a multiple of 3".

The given statement is of the form $p \rightarrow q$.

The negation of an implication $p \rightarrow q$ is given by $\sim(p \rightarrow q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q$.

Therefore, the negation of the given statement is "An integer is greater than 4 and less than 5 but it is not a multiple of 3".

Answer: An integer is greater than 4 and less than 5 but it is not a multiple of 3.

65537.subject: Physics
65537.text: Which graph shows the correct variation of r.m.s. current '$i$' with frequency '$f$' of a.c. in case of series resonant circuit ?
65537.sol:
In a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by:

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(X_L - X_C\right)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(2\pi f L - \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}\right)^2}$

The r.m.s. current is:

$i = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z}$

At the resonant frequency $f_r = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance (X_L = X_C$). At this point, the impedance $Z$ is minimum (Z = R$) and the current $i$ is maximum.

For frequencies $f < f_r$, $Z$ is large and $i$ is small. As $f$ increases towards $f_r$, $Z$ decreases and $i$ increases.
For frequencies $f > f_r$, $Z$ increases again and $i$ decreases.

Thus, the graph of current $i$ versus frequency $f$ is a bell-shaped curve with a peak at the resonant frequency. Graph (P) correctly represents this variation.

Answer: $(P)$

68019.text: Two vectors $a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other. When $3 a+2 b=7$, the ratio of $a$ to $b$ is $\frac{x}{2}$. The value of $x$ is
68019.sol:
Given vectors $\mathrm{V_1} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\mathrm{V_2} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ are perpendicular, so their dot product equals zero: $2a - 3b + 4 = 0$
This simplifies to $2a - 3b = -4$

The second condition gives $3a + 2b = 7$

Solving this system by elimination, multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3:

$4a - 6b = -8$
$9a + 6b = 21$

Adding eliminates $b$ and yields $13a = 13$, so $a = 1$

Substituting into $3a + 2b = 7$ gives $3 + 2b = 7$, hence $b = 2$

The ratio $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{1}{2}$ equals $\frac{x}{2}$, so $x = 1$

Answer: $\boxed{C}$

$T = \dfrac{48 \times 2.5}{4}$

$T = 12 \times 2.5 = 30$ dyne/cm

69168.subject: Physics
69168.text: A thin uniform rod of length $2$ m cross-sectional area 'A' and density 'd' is rotated about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to its length with angular velocity $\omega$. If the value of $\omega$ in terms of its rotational kinetic energy $E$ is $(\alpha E/Ad)^{1/2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ is
69168.sol:
Mass of the rod, $M = \text{Volume} \times \text{density} = A \times L \times d$

Given $L = 2$, $M = 2Ad$

Moment of inertia of the rod about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length is $I = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}$

Substituting the values of $M$ and $L$, we get $I = \dfrac{2Ad \times 2^2}{12} = \dfrac{2Ad}{3}$

Rotational kinetic energy is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

Substituting the value of $I$, $E = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{2Ad}{3} \right) \omega^2 = \dfrac{Ad}{3} \omega^2$

Rearranging for $\omega$, we get $\omega = \left( \dfrac{3E}{Ad} \right)^{1/2}$

Comparing this with the given expression $\omega = \left( \dfrac{\alpha E}{Ad} \right)^{1/2}$, we find $\alpha = 3$.

Answer: $3$

69701.subject: Physics
69701.text: Two rods of same length, radius and material transfer a given amount of heat in 't' second when they are joined as shown in fig (1). But when they are joined as shown in fig (2) then they will transfer same heat in same condition in time
69701.sol:
Let the thermal resistance of each rod be $R$.

In figure (1), the two rods are connected in parallel. The equivalent thermal resistance is:
$R_p = \dfrac{R \times R}{R + R} = \dfrac{R}{2}$

The amount of heat transferred in time $t$ is:
$Q = \dfrac{\Delta T}{R_p} t = \dfrac{2 \Delta T}{R} t$

In figure (2), the two rods are connected in series. The equivalent thermal resistance is:
$R_s = R + R = 2R$

Let the time taken to transfer the same amount of heat $Q$ under the same temperature difference $\Delta T$ be $t'$. Then:
$Q = \dfrac{\Delta T}{R_s} t' = \dfrac{\Delta T}{2R} t'$

Equating the two expressions for $Q$:
$\dfrac{2 \Delta T}{R} t = \dfrac{\Delta T}{2R} t'$

$2t = \dfrac{t'}{2}$

$t' = 4t$

Answer: $4t$

69969.subject: Physics
69969.text: A diatomic gas $\left(\gamma=\frac{7}{5}\right)$ is compressed adiabatically to volume $\frac{\mathrm{v}_0}{32}$, where $V_0$ is its initial volume. The initial temperature of the gas is $T_i$ in kelvin and the final temperature is $\mathrm{xT}_{\mathrm{i}}$ in kelvin. The value of x is
69969.sol:
For an adiabatic process with diatomic gas ($\gamma = 7/5$), the temperature-volume relation $T V^{\gamma-1} = \text{constant}$ applies.

Given initial conditions $V_i = V_0$, $T_i$ and final conditions $V_f = V_0/32$, $T_f = x T_i$, the adiabatic relation becomes:

$T_i V_0^{2/5} = x T_i (V_0/32)^{2/5}$

Dividing both sides by $T_i V_0^{2/5}$ yields $1 = x / 32^{2/5}$.

Since $32 = 2^5$, we have $32^{2/5} = (2^5)^{2/5} = 2^2 = 4$.

Thus $x = 4$, corresponding to option B.

71002.text: The volume of air remaining in the lungs and the dead space even after maximum expiration is ----------ml.
71002.sol:
The volume of air remaining in the lungs and the respiratory passages (dead space) even after a forceful or maximum expiration is called the Residual Volume (RV).

The average value of Residual Volume in a healthy human adult is $1100$ mL to $1200$ mL.

Other respiratory volumes are:
Tidal Volume (TV) $\approx 500$ mL
Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) $\approx 1000$ to $1100$ mL
Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) $\approx 2500$ to $3000$ mL

Answer: 1100-1200

71082.subject: Biology
71082.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Analogous organs leads to convergent evolution.
Statement (II): Analogous organs help to trace common ancestry.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false.
Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false.
Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true.
71082.sol:
Statement (I) is false because analogous organs are the result of convergent evolution, they do not lead to convergent evolution. Convergent evolution is the process by which unrelated or distantly related organisms evolve similar body forms, coloration, or organs due to adapting to similar environments.

Statement (II) is false because analogous organs do not indicate common ancestry. It is homologous organs (organs with similar fundamental structure but different functions) that help to trace common ancestry, as they arise due to divergent evolution from a common ancestor.

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false.

71541.subject: Biology
71541.text:
Assertion - (A) The hepatic portal vein exhibits a wide lumen and comparatively thinner tunica media.
Reason - (R) Its endothelial lining is arranged in a tessellated pattern to facilitate exchange between blood and hepatocytes.
Choose the correct option from the following.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation for (A).
(A) is true; however, statement (R) is false.
71541.sol:
The hepatic portal vein is a blood vessel that carries blood from the gastrointestinal tract, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen to the liver. Like other veins, it has a wider lumen and a comparatively thinner tunica media than arteries. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

The exchange of materials between the blood and hepatocytes does not occur across the walls of the hepatic portal vein. Instead, the hepatic portal vein branches into smaller venules that eventually empty into the hepatic sinusoids. The hepatic sinusoids are highly permeable capillaries with fenestrated endothelial linings that facilitate the actual exchange of substances between the blood and hepatocytes. Therefore, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true; however, statement (R) is false.

72034.subject: Chemistry
72034.text:
$500\ \text{mL}$ of nitrogen gas and $750\ \text{mL}$ hydrogen gas were allowed to react at $1\ \text{bar}$ pressure according to reaction,
$\text{N}_{2(g)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_{3(g)}$
What is PV type of work done during reaction?
72034.sol:
The given reaction is $\text{N}_{2(g)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_{3(g)}$.

Initial volume of $\text{N}_2 = 500\ \text{mL}$
Initial volume of $\text{H}_2 = 750\ \text{mL}$
Total initial volume $V_i = 500 + 750 = 1250\ \text{mL}$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ volume of $\text{N}_2$ reacts with $3$ volumes of $\text{H}_2$ to produce $2$ volumes of $\text{NH}_3$.

Here, $\text{H}_2$ is the limiting reagent. $750\ \text{mL}$ of $\text{H}_2$ will react with $250\ \text{mL}$ of $\text{N}_2$ to form $500\ \text{mL}$ of $\text{NH}_3$.

Volume of $\text{N}_2$ remaining $= 500 - 250 = 250\ \text{mL}$
Total final volume $V_f = 250\ (\text{N}_2) + 500\ (\text{NH}_3) = 750\ \text{mL}$

Change in volume $\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 750 - 1250 = -500\ \text{mL} = -0.5\ \text{L}$

Work done $W = -P_{ext} \Delta V$

$W = -1\ \text{bar} \times (-0.5\ \text{L}) = +0.5\ \text{L}\ \text{bar}$

Since $1\ \text{L}\ \text{bar} = 100\ \text{J}$,

$W = +0.5 \times 100\ \text{J} = +50\ \text{J}$

Answer: $+50\ \text{J}$

72244.subject: Physics
72244.text: A vessel is filled with a gas at a pressure of 76 cm of mercury at a certain temperature. The mass of the gas is increased by 75 % by introducing more gas in the vessel at the same temperature. The resultant pressure of the gas is
72244.sol:
From the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT = \dfrac{m}{M}RT$.

Since the volume $V$ of the vessel and the temperature $T$ remain constant, the pressure of the gas is directly proportional to its mass $m$.

$P \propto m$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = \dfrac{m_2}{m_1}$

Given that the mass of the gas is increased by $75\%$, the final mass is:

$m_2 = m_1 + 0.75m_1 = 1.75m_1$

Substituting the values into the pressure relation:

$\dfrac{P_2}{76} = \dfrac{1.75m_1}{m_1}$

$P_2 = 1.75 \times 76 = 133$ cm of Hg.

Answer: 133 cm of mercury

72267.subject: Physics
72267.text: A circular loop carrying a current' I' is made of a wire of length 'L'. A uniform magnetic field 'B' exists parallel to the plane of the loop. The torque experienced by the circular loop will be
72267.sol:
The length of the wire is $L$. For a circular loop, the circumference is equal to $L$.

$2\pi R = L \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$

The area of the circular loop is given by:

$A = \pi R^2 = \pi \left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{4\pi}$

The magnetic dipole moment of the current-carrying loop is:

$M = IA = \dfrac{IL^2}{4\pi}$

The magnetic field $B$ is parallel to the plane of the loop, which means the angle $\theta$ between the area vector (magnetic moment $\vec{M}$) and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The torque experienced by the loop is:

$\tau = MB \sin\theta = \left(\dfrac{IL^2}{4\pi}\right) B \sin(90^{{}^{\circ}})$

$\tau = \dfrac{IL^2B}{4\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{IL^2B}{4\pi}$

72292.text: If $\vec{A} = \vec{B} + \vec{C}$ and magnitudes of $\vec{A}, \vec{B}$ and $\vec{C}$ are 5, 4 and 3 units respectively. The angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$ is
72292.sol:
Given $\vec{A} = \vec{B} + \vec{C}$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$\vec{B} = \vec{A} - \vec{C}$

Taking the dot product of $\vec{B}$ with itself:

$|\vec{B}|^2 = |\vec{A} - \vec{C}|^2$

$|\vec{B}|^2 = |\vec{A}|^2 + |\vec{C}|^2 - 2|\vec{A}||\vec{C}|\cos\theta$

where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$.

Substituting the given magnitudes A = 5$, $B = 4$, and $C = 3$:

4^2 = 5^2 + 3^2 - 2(5)(3)\cos\theta$

$16 = 25 + 9 - 30\cos\theta$

$16 = 34 - 30\cos\theta$

$30\cos\theta = 18$

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{18}{30} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$\theta = \cos^{-1} \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)

Answer: \cos^{-1}\left({3}/{5}\right)$

Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions on $[0,2]$ satisfying $\mathrmf^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrmg^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x}), \mathrmf^{\prime}(1)=4, \mathrm{ g}^{\prime}(1)=6, f(2)=3$ and $g(2)=9$. Then what is $f(x)-g(x)$ at $x=4$ equal to ?
77501.sol:
$f^{\prime \prime}(x)=g^{\prime \prime}(x)$
integrate b|s w.r.t. (x)
$f^{\prime}(x)+C_1=g^{\prime}(x)+C_2$...(1)
Putting $x=1\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(1)+C_1=g^{\prime}(1)+C_2 \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=g^{\prime}(1)-f^{\prime}(1) \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=6-4=2
\end{aligned}$
again integrating equation (1)
$f(x)+C_1 x+a_1=g(x)+C_2 x+a_2$...(3)
Putting $x=2\begin{aligned}
& f(2)+C_1 \times 2+a_1=g(2)+2 C_2+a_2 \\
& \Rightarrow a_1-a_2=g(2)+2 C_2-2 C_1-f(2) \\
& \quad=9-3-2\left(C_1-C_2\right) \\
& \quad=6-2 \times 2=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}_1-\mathrm{a}_2=2
\end{aligned}$
Rearranging equation (3) again, we get
$f(x)-g(x)=-x \left(C_1-C_2\right)-  \left(a_1-a_2\right)$
Putting $x=4$, we get
\begin{aligned}
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } $=-4\left(C_1-C_2\right)-\left(a_1-a_2\right) \\
& =-4 \times(2)-2 \\
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } & =-10
\end{aligned}$

77917.text: How many 5-digit prime numbers can be formed using the digits $1,2,3,4,5$ if the repetition of digits is not allowed?
77917.sol:
Any 5-digits number formed by the digits 1,2,3,4 and 5 (without repetition) will be always divisible by number 3 , because sum of digits of any number, thus formed $1+2+3+4+5=15$, is divisible by 3.
Hence, prime number of 5 digits can not be obtained by using the digits $1,2,3,4,5$.

79582.subject: Botany
79582.sol:
ARCHAEBACTERIA:

These archaebacteria are special since they live in some of the harshest habitats such as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles), and marshy areas (methanogens).
Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

Archaebacteria are divided into three groups - methanogens, halophiles, and thermoacidophiles.

Methanogens: These bacteria are of marshy habitats. They are capable of converting CO2, methanol, and formic acid into methane so named methanogens. These methanogens are present in the guts of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes, and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals. These are chemoautotrophs.
Examples: Methanococcus, Methanobacterium, etc.

central region of style through which the pollen tube grows towards the ovary
endodermis of roots facilitating rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle.
80662.sol: The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. Endodermis is a single layered structure which separates cortex from stele. There are both thick walled and thin-walled cells in the endodermis. The thin-walled cells are known as passage cells or transfusion cells which are opposite the protoxylem groups. These cells help in rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle. Related Theory Apoplast includes the non-living components of a plant such as cell walls and the intracellular spaces. In contrast, in the symplast pathway, water moves by the osmosis since water moves across the cell membranes. (Ref. to Fig. 25.4)

83224.text: The power obtained in a reactor using $\mathrm{U}^{235}$ disintegration is $1000 \mathrm{~kW}$. The mass decay of $\mathrm{U}^{235}$ per hour is
83224.sol:
Let assume power $P=1000 \mathrm{~W}$
Energy per hour $=1000 \times 3600 \mathrm{~J}$
Energy per fission $=200 \mathrm{MeV}=200 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J}\therefore$ Number of fission per hour
$n=\frac{1000 \times 3600}{200 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13}} \begin{aligned}
& \text{Number of mole per hour }=\frac{n}{N} \\
& \therefore \text{ Mass per hour }=\frac{n}{N} \times 235
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1000 \times 3600 \times 235}{200 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \times 6.02 \times 10^{23}} \\
& =43.9 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~g}
\end{aligned}$
This $43.9 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~g}$ is nearest value of 40 micro gram so option (b) is correct.

$

Let us assume that just after the collision, the speed of the particle plus $1$ kg block is $u$

$2u = 1 \times 10 ⇒ u = 5ms^{- 1}$

After the collision and until the string is taut again, the particle block system is in free fall. So just before the string is taut, the particle plus $1$ kg block will be moving downward with a velocity of $5ms^{- 1}$ and just after the string is taut, let us assume that the speed of both the blocks and the particle is $v$, then

$2 \times 5 = 5v$

$⇒ v = 2ms^{- 1}$

96547.text: Identify the correct sequence of involvement, according to ecological succession.
96547.sol: The gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area is called ecological succession. During succession some species colonise an area and whereas populations of other species decline and even disappear. The entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area are called sere(s). The individual transitional communities are termed seral stages or seral communities. Ultimately a stable climax forest community is formed. The climax community remains stable as long as the environment remains unchanged.

98361.subject: Chemistry
98361.text: The given structure of protein corresponds to:
98361.sol:
Structure of protein has upto 4 levels :

$1.$ Primary structure - Linear sequence of amino acids with 2 terminals :

A. N- terminal : On left side and is represented by the first amino acid (also known as N- terminal amino acid).

B. C- terminal : On right side and is represented by the last amino acid (also known as C- terminal amino acid).

- This structure appears like a thread and is non-functional.

$2.$ Secondary structure - The above mentioned thread is folded in staircase like helix at some portions and in some other forms in remaining portions. This is also non-functional structure.

$3.$ Tertiary structure - Long chain is also folded upon itself to form a hollow woolen ball like structure. To be functional to perform biological activity, proteins should acquire at least tertiary structure.

$4.$ Quaternary structure - Few proteins are made up of 2 or more polypeptides because of which one more arrangement is there between them with respect to each other. This is termed as quaternary structure.

Example: Adult haemoglobin is made up of 4 globulin chains - 2α chains and 2β chains.

100890.subject: Physics
100890.text: A particle of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ moves along the positive $x$-axis under the action of a position-dependent force $F$. The force increases linearly from $0$ to $10 \text{ N}$ between $x = 0$ and $x = 2 \text{ m}$, remains constant at $10 \text{ N}$ from $x = 2 \text{ m}$ to $x = 4 \text{ m}$, and then remains constant at $-5 \text{ N}$ from $x = 4 \text{ m}$ to $x = 8 \text{ m}$. If the initial velocity of the particle at $x = 0$ is $4 \text{ m/s}$, the kinetic energy of the particle at $x = 8 \text{ m}$ is
100890.sol:
According to the work-energy theorem, the net work done by the force equals the change in kinetic energy of the particle: $W_{\text{net}} = K_f - K_i$.

The initial kinetic energy is:
$K_i = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (4)^2 = 16 \text{ J}$

The work done is the algebraic sum of the areas under the force-position graph:
Work from $x = 0$ to $x = 2 \text{ m}$ (area of triangle) = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10 = 10 \text{ J}$
Work from $x = 2$ to $x = 4 \text{ m}$ (area of rectangle) = $2 \times 10 = 20 \text{ J}$
Work from $x = 4$ to $x = 8 \text{ m}$ (area of rectangle) = $4 \times (-5) = -20 \text{ J}$

Total work done $W_{\text{net}} = 10 + 20 - 20 = 10 \text{ J}$.

Using the work-energy theorem:
$K_f - 16 = 10$
$K_f = 26 \text{ J}$

Answer: 26 J

101021.subject: Physics
101021.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
101021.text: Two particles of masses $m$ and $2m$ start moving simultaneously from the same point on a smooth horizontal circular track in opposite directions. Both particles move with the same constant speed $v$. What is the magnitude of the total linear momentum of the two-particle system at the instant when each particle has covered an angular distance of $45^{\circ}$ from the starting point?
101021.sol:
Let the particles start from the point $(R, 0)$ on a circular track of radius $R$ centered at the origin.

The first particle (mass $m$) moves counter-clockwise. When it covers an angular distance of $45^{\circ}$, its position vector makes an angle of $+45^{\circ}$ with the x-axis. Its velocity vector is tangential to the circular path, making an angle of $45^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$ with the positive x-axis.

The second particle (mass $2m$) moves clockwise. When it covers an angular distance of $45^{\circ}$, its position vector makes an angle of $-45^{\circ}$ with the x-axis. Its velocity vector is tangential, making an angle of $-45^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} = -135^{\circ}$ with the positive x-axis.

The angle between the two velocity vectors is $135^{\circ} - (-135^{\circ}) = 270^{\circ}$, which is geometrically equivalent to $90^{\circ}$. Thus, the velocity vectors are perpendicular to each other.

The magnitude of the linear momentum of the first particle is $p_1 = mv$.

The magnitude of the linear momentum of the second particle is $p_2 = 2mv$.

Since the two momentum vectors are perpendicular, the magnitude of the total linear momentum of the system is the vector sum:
$P = \sqrt{p_1^2 + p_2^2} = \sqrt{(mv)^2 + (2mv)^2} = \sqrt{m^2v^2 + 4m^2v^2} = \sqrt{5}mv$.

Answer: $\sqrt{5}mv$

102070.subject: Physics
102070.text: Two vertical cylinders are placed in a vacuum chamber and contain ideal gases. They are fitted with heavy, frictionless movable pistons. The piston of cylinder $A$ has mass $m$ and radius $r$, while the piston of cylinder $B$ has mass $2m$ and radius $2r$. Equal amounts of heat are supplied to both gases, and they undergo an expansion such that the change in their internal energies is the same. The ratio of the upward displacement of piston $A$ to that of piston $B$ ($x_A : x_B$) is:
102070.sol:
From the First Law of Thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$.

Since $Q_A = Q_B$ and $\Delta U_A = \Delta U_B$, the work done by both gases must be equal ($W_A = W_B$).

In a vacuum chamber, the external atmospheric pressure is zero. The pressure of the gas is purely due to the weight of the piston: $P = \dfrac{mg}{\pi r^2}$.

The work done by the gas during an upward displacement $x$ is $W = P \Delta V = \left(\dfrac{mg}{\pi r^2}\right) (\pi r^2 x) = mgx$.

Notice that the work done is simply the change in gravitational potential energy of the piston, which is independent of the piston's radius.

Equating the work done for both cylinders:
$m_A g x_A = m_B g x_B$

103691.subject: Physics
103691.text: A straight wire of mass $200 \text{ g}$ and length $5 \text{ m}$ carries a current of $2 \text{ A}$. It is oriented horizontally along the vector $\vec{L} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$ (in meters). The wire is suspended in mid-air, balancing gravity which acts in the $-\hat{k}$ direction, by a uniform magnetic field of the form $\vec{B} = B_0\hat{i} + B_0\hat{j} + B_z\hat{k}$. What is the required magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
103691.sol:
The gravitational force on the wire is $\vec{W} = -mg\hat{k} = -0.2 \times 10 \hat{k} = -2\hat{k} \text{ N}$.

For the wire to be in mechanical equilibrium, the magnetic force must balance the weight:
$\vec{F}_m = +2\hat{k} \text{ N}$

The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is given by $\vec{F}_m = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})$.
Here, $I = 2 \text{ A}$ and $\vec{L} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$.

Calculating the cross product:
$\vec{F}_m = 2 [ (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \times (B_0\hat{i} + B_0\hat{j} + B_z\hat{k}) ]$
$\vec{F}_m = 2 [ 3B_0(\hat{i} \times \hat{i}) + 3B_0(\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + 3B_z(\hat{i} \times \hat{k}) + 4B_0(\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) + 4B_0(\hat{j} \times \hat{j}) + 4B_z(\hat{j} \times \hat{k}) ]$
$\vec{F}_m = 2 [ 0 + 3B_0\hat{k} - 3B_z\hat{j} - 4B_0\hat{k} + 0 + 4B_z\hat{i} ]$
$\vec{F}_m = 8B_z\hat{i} - 6B_z\hat{j} - 2B_0\hat{k}$

Equating this to the required force $+2\hat{k}$:
$8B_z\hat{i} - 6B_z\hat{j} - 2B_0\hat{k} = 0\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

Comparing the components:
$8B_z = 0 \Rightarrow B_z = 0$
$-2B_0 = 2 \Rightarrow B_0 = -1 \text{ T}$

Therefore, the complete magnetic field vector is $\vec{B} = -\hat{i} - \hat{j}$.

Balancing gravity with the wrong sign would incorrectly yield $\hat{i} + \hat{j}$, while forgetting to multiply by the current $I$ would yield $-2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$.

Answer: $-\hat{i} - \hat{j}$

103719.subject: Physics
103719.text: A uniform circular wire loop of radius $R$ is bent along its diameter so that the two semicircular halves lie in mutually perpendicular planes. A steady total current $I$ enters the loop at one end of the common diameter and leaves at the other end. The magnitude of the net magnetic field at the centre of the bent loop is:
103719.sol:
Since the wire loop is uniform, the two semicircular halves have equal resistance. When the total current $I$ enters at one end of the diameter, it divides equally into the two parallel branches.
Current in each semicircle = $\dfrac{I}{2}$.

The magnetic field at the centre due to a semicircle carrying current $i$ is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}$.
For the first semicircle:
$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 (I/2)}{4R} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8R}$
This field is directed perpendicular to the plane of the first semicircle.

For the second semicircle:
$B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 (I/2)}{4R} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8R}$
This field is directed perpendicular to the plane of the second semicircle.

Because the two semicircles lie in mutually perpendicular planes, their magnetic field vectors $\vec{B}_1$ and $\vec{B}_2$ at the centre are also mutually perpendicular (angle between them is $90^{\circ}$).

The net magnetic field is the vector sum of $\vec{B}_1$ and $\vec{B}_2$:
$B_{net} = \sqrt{B_1^2 + B_2^2} = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8R}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8R}\right)^2} = \sqrt{2} \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8R}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{8R}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{8R}$

104283.subject: Physics
104283.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For an electromagnetic wave propagating in a non-magnetic medium with relative permittivity $\epsilon_r = 4$, if the electric field amplitude is $E_0$, the corresponding magnetic field amplitude is $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{2c}$ (where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum).

Reason (R): The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$, and the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = v B_0$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
104283.sol:
The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.
For a non-magnetic medium, the relative permeability $\mu_r = 1$. Given $\epsilon_r = 4$, the speed of the wave is $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{1 \times 4}} = \dfrac{c}{2}$.

The amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = v B_0$.
Substituting the value of $v$, we get $E_0 = \left(\dfrac{c}{2}\right) B_0$, which gives $B_0 = \dfrac{2E_0}{c}$.

The Assertion incorrectly states that $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{2c}$. The Reason correctly states the standard formulas for wave speed and the amplitude relation. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

105256.subject: Physics
105256.text: An oscilloscope monitoring a logic circuit shows that the output $Y$ drops to a logic LOW ($0$) state if and only if both inputs $A$ and $B$ are simultaneously at a logic HIGH ($1$) state. At all other times, the output $Y$ remains at a logic HIGH ($1$) state. Which of the following Boolean expressions correctly represents the relationship between the inputs and the output?
105256.sol:
From the given description, the output $Y = 0$ only when $A = 1$ and $B = 1$. For all other combinations ($(0,0), (0,1), (1,0)$), the output $Y = 1$.

This behavior corresponds exactly to the truth table of a NAND gate.

The Boolean expression for a NAND gate is $Y = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

According to De Morgan's theorem, the complement of a product is equal to the sum of the complements:
$\overline{A \cdot B} = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$

Therefore, the correct Boolean expression is $Y = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$.

Answer: $Y = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$

108679.subject: Chemistry
108679.text:
The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate is given by the following equation:
$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{CaO(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$
At $1000$ K, the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\ominus}$) for this reaction is $+22.6$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the standard entropy change ($\Delta S^{\ominus}$) is $+160$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
What is the standard internal energy change ($\Delta U^{\ominus}$) for the reaction at $1000$ K?
(Given: $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
108679.sol:
First, calculate the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{\ominus}$) using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - T \Delta S^{\ominus}$

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta G^{\ominus} + T \Delta S^{\ominus}$

Substituting the given values (converting $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ to kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$):

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = 22.6 + 1000 \times (160 \times 10^{-3})$

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = 22.6 + 160 = +182.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Next, determine the change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta n_g$). Only $\text{CO}_2$ is gaseous:

$\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = 1$

Now, calculate the standard internal energy change ($\Delta U^{\ominus}$) using the relation:

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R T$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = 182.6 - (1) \times (8.3 \times 10^{-3}) \times 1000$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = 182.6 - 8.3 = +174.3 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $+174.3$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

108958.subject: Chemistry
108958.text:
In the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia, $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is $4.0 \times 10^{-4}$ at $500\text{ K}$. If the backward reaction rate constant $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}$ at this temperature is $2.0 \times 10^{-2}$, what is the value of the forward reaction rate constant $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$?

[Given: $\mathrm{R} = 0.08\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
108958.sol:
For the reaction $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$

The relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}$

Rearranging to solve for $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}}{(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}(\mathrm{RT})^2$

Calculate $\mathrm{RT}$:
$\mathrm{RT} = 0.08 \times 500 = 40$

Now, substitute the values to find $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = (4.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times (40)^2 = (4.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times 1600 = 0.64$

The equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is also given by the ratio of the forward and backward rate constants:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}$

Solving for $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$:
$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} \times \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.64 \times (2.0 \times 10^{-2}) = 1.28 \times 10^{-2}$

Answer: $1.28 \times 10^{-2}$

112637.subject: Chemistry
112637.text: Which of the following alkanes can be readily oxidized to an alcohol by potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$)?
112637.sol:
Generally, alkanes are inert towards strong oxidizing agents such as $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$. However, alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom are an exception and can be oxidized to the corresponding tertiary alcohols.

Let us examine the structures of the given alkanes:
1) 2-Methylbutane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$. The carbon at position 2 is a tertiary carbon, so it possesses a tertiary hydrogen atom.
2) $n$-Butane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$. It contains only primary and secondary hydrogen atoms.
3) 2,2-Dimethylpropane: $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_4$. It contains a quaternary carbon and primary hydrogen atoms, but no tertiary hydrogen.
4) $n$-Hexane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-(\mathrm{CH}_2)_4-\mathrm{CH}_3$. It contains only primary and secondary hydrogen atoms.

Thus, only 2-Methylbutane will be oxidized by $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ to form 2-Methylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: 2-Methylbutane

113926.subject: Chemistry
113926.text: The molality of an aqueous solution of urea is $3 \text{ m}$. If the density of the solution is $1.18 \text{ g/mL}$, the molarity of the solution is [Given: Molar mass of urea $= 60 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
113926.sol:
Given, molality $= 3 \text{ m}$, which means $3 \text{ moles}$ of urea are present in $1 \text{ kg}$ ($1000 \text{ g}$) of solvent (water).

Mass of solvent $= 1000 \text{ g}$
Molar mass of urea $= 60 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Mass of urea (solute) $= \text{moles} \times \text{molar mass} = 3 \times 60 = 180 \text{ g}$

Total mass of the solution $= \text{Mass of solvent} + \text{Mass of solute}$
Total mass of solution $= 1000 \text{ g} + 180 \text{ g} = 1180 \text{ g}$

Given density of solution $= 1.18 \text{ g/mL}$
Volume of solution $= \dfrac{\text{Mass of solution}}{\text{Density}} = \dfrac{1180 \text{ g}}{1.18 \text{ g/mL}} = 1000 \text{ mL} = 1 \text{ L}$

Molarity $= \dfrac{\text{Number of moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution (in L)}}$
Molarity $= \dfrac{3 \text{ mol}}{1 \text{ L}} = 3.00 \text{ M}$

Answer: $3.00 \text{ M}$

114388.subject: Chemistry
114388.text:
Calculate the emf of the cell in which the following spontaneous reaction takes place at $298 \text{ K}$:

$2Fe^{3+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq) \rightarrow 2Fe^{2+}(aq) + I_2(s)$

Given:
$E^\circ_{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}} = 0.77 \text{ V}$
$E^\circ_{I_2/I^-} = 0.54 \text{ V}$
$[Fe^{3+}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$
$[Fe^{2+}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$
$[I^-] = 0.1 \text{ M}$
$\left( \text{Take } \dfrac{2.303 RT}{F} = 0.059 \text{ at } 298 \text{ K} \right)$
114388.sol:
The standard cell potential is calculated from the standard reduction potentials:
$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode} = 0.77 \text{ V} - 0.54 \text{ V} = 0.23 \text{ V}$

The balanced redox reaction involves the transfer of $n = 2$ electrons.
The reaction quotient $Q$ is given by:
$Q = \dfrac{[Fe^{2+}]^2}{[Fe^{3+}]^2 [I^-]^2}$ (since solid $I_2$ has an active mass of 1)

Substituting the given concentrations:
$Q = \dfrac{(0.1)^2}{(0.01)^2 (0.1)^2} = \dfrac{10^{-2}}{10^{-4} \times 10^{-2}} = \dfrac{10^{-2}}{10^{-6}} = 10^4$

Applying the Nernst equation:
$E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log Q$
$E_{cell} = 0.23 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log(10^4)$
$E_{cell} = 0.23 - 0.0295 \times 4$
$E_{cell} = 0.23 - 0.118 = 0.112 \text{ V}$

Answer: $0.112 \text{ V}$

121730.subject: Botany
121730.text: What is the size range of brown algae?
121730.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, <mark>filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters.</mark> They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf-like photosynthetic organ – the frond. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.

121825.subject: Botany
121825.text: What do the megaspores and microspores give rise to, respectively?
121825.sol: Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. <mark>The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively.</mark> The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit considered an important step in evolution. The pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

122024.subject: Botany
122024.text: Read the following statements regarding the male gametophyte in gymnosperms and choose the incorrect statement.
options: The male gametophytes are carried by water currents to the mouth of the archegonia.
It develops from a microspore within the microsporangium.
It is highly reduced and is confined to only a limited number of cells, called a pollen grain.
It does not have an independent, free-living existence and remains retained within the sporangia.
122024.sol:
In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.

The microspores develop into a highly reduced male gametophyte called a pollen grain. The development of pollen grains takes place within the microsporangia.

Once released from the microsporangium, the pollen grains are carried by air currents, not water currents. They come in contact with the opening of the ovules borne on megasporophylls, where the pollen tube grows towards the archegonia.

Thus, the statement claiming they are carried by water currents is incorrect.

Answer: The male gametophytes are carried by water currents to the mouth of the archegonia.

123439.subject: Botany
123439.text: Which of the following pairs of tissue descriptions and their corresponding examples is incorrectly matched?
options: Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Phloem in angiosperms
Tissue with active cell division : Intercalary meristem in grasses
Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen : Sclereids in pulp of guava
Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Parenchyma in cortex
123439.sol:
According to NCERT, simple tissues are made of only one type of cells (all cells similar in structure and function), such as parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma. Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells and work together as a unit. Phloem is a complex tissue, not a simple tissue. In angiosperms, phloem is composed of four different types of cells: sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

Intercalary meristem in grasses is a meristematic tissue capable of active cell division. Parenchyma in the cortex is a simple tissue. Sclereids in the pulp of guava are dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow cavities.

Answer: Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Phloem in angiosperms

125630.subject: Botany
125630.text: In plants possessing Kranz anatomy, photorespiration is virtually absent. Which of the following mechanisms specifically ensures that RuBisCO functions primarily as a carboxylase in these plants?
options: Mesophyll cells actively pump gaseous $\mathrm{CO}_2$ directly into the bundle sheath cells to saturate the enzyme.
RuBisCO in these plants structurally lacks an oxygenase active site, preventing any binding with oxygen.
Decarboxylation of $\mathrm{C}_4$ acids in the bundle sheath cells creates a high intracellular concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$.
PEPcase acts as a physical shield around RuBisCO in the mesophyll cells, blocking oxygen entry.
125630.sol:
In $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants (which possess Kranz anatomy), photorespiration does not occur. This is because they have a mechanism that increases the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at the enzyme site.

This takes place when the $\mathrm{C}_4$ acid (like malic or aspartic acid) from the mesophyll is broken down (decarboxylated) in the bundle sheath cells to release $\mathrm{CO}_2$. This results in increasing the intracellular concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$, which ensures that RuBisCO functions as a carboxylase minimizing the oxygenase activity.

The enzyme RuBisCO itself is identical to that in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants, and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is transported as $\mathrm{C}_4$ acids, not as a free gas. Furthermore, RuBisCO is located in the bundle sheath cells, not mesophyll cells.

Answer: Decarboxylation of $\mathrm{C}_4$ acids in the bundle sheath cells creates a high intracellular concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$.

125672.subject: Botany
125672.text:
Match List I with List II regarding photosynthetic pathways.

List IList II
A. RuBisCO in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plantsI. Mesophyll cells
B. RuBisCO in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plantsII. Bundle sheath cells
C. PEPcase in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plantsIII. Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP)
D. Primary $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plantsIV. Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
125672.sol:
In $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants, the Calvin cycle occurs in the mesophyll cells, so the enzyme RuBisCO is localized there.

In $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants, there is a spatial separation of pathways. The initial fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ occurs in the mesophyll cells where the enzyme PEPcase is present. The Calvin cycle operates in the bundle sheath cells, which is where RuBisCO is localized.

The primary $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants is a 5-carbon ketose sugar, Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-I, D-IV. Matching PEPcase to PEP is a common mistake, but PEP is a substrate, not a cellular location.

Answer: A-I, B-II, C-I, D-IV

125673.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Photorespiration does not occur in $\text{C}_4$ plants.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
